title: SPHEREx shows the 3.1 um ice band of Gaia20cdd in three visits over 12 months at a normal 1 um flux, but no such band in 88 other dimmers or 206 extreme-dust dwarfs
abstract: We measured the 3.1 um water-ice band in SPHEREx Quick Release 2 and 3 images (2025 April to 2026 October) for 94 main-sequence dimmers (81 TZ25 dippers and 13 campaign dimmers), 208 unblended field dwarfs with extreme 12 um excess and 227 matched field controls. We made forced PSF photometry on 34,375 exposures, read as small pixel boxes from the AWS mirror of the IRSA archive. For each band exposure we also measured the simultaneous 0.75-1.1 um exposure, to test if the star was in a dip. Gaia20cdd has a band in all three visits (2025 July 0.233 +- 0.040, 2025 December 0.312 +- 0.031, 2026 July 0.255 +- 0.037; mean 0.275 +- 0.020, 13.8 sigma), while its simultaneous 1 um flux stays within 3 percent of the visit level. Thus its icy screen persisted for at least a year and is not a short dip; at 12 km/s or more it is at least 2.5 au long. After calibration with the controls, no other dimmer (0 of 88) and no extreme-dust dwarf (0 of 206) has a band above 4 sigma. A Gaia20cdd-like band was excluded at 5 sigma in 57 TZ25 dippers and 205 extreme-dust dwarfs, so fewer than 5.3 and 1.5 percent (95 percent limits) had such a persistent screen. One apparent 7.3 sigma band (TZ25_560384) was a grey dip that SPHEREx sampled only in the band exposures. Field M dwarfs show a photospheric pseudo-band of 0.03-0.07, and a weak +0.005 offset of the extreme-dust stars follows their hot-dust continuum slope. Limitations: the census tests quiet states, few dips were sampled, Quick Release calibration is preliminary, and the M-dwarf control locus has 12 stars.
